source.title: Representations converge as brain maps diverge along the cortical hierarchy
source.authors: B. Petre; M. Lindquist; T. Wager

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests convergence across independently initialized networks using CKA and related representational-geometry measures, rather than reproducing the cited studies' methods. It also compares a spatial wiring penalty with task-only training.
record.gate_note: The paper measures representational similarity across independently initialized ANN dyads and reports how it varies with network layer and wiring penalty. Its brain results are analogous findings in people, not tests of the AI-model versions; they are recorded under fits_no_version. Classification agreement is a functional outcome, not a direct representation-similarity result.
record.test_reason: The study trains 14 ResNet-18 seeds per class (with and without a spatial wiring loss) on ImageNet contrastive self-supervision. It measures cross-seed representational similarity with linear CKA (0.91) alongside unit-level topographic cosine (0.36). This bears on V3, convergence across seeds with different units, using a different method from Li et al.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that seed-varied ANNs converge in representations (CKA 0.91) despite divergent topographies, and that wiring cost aids topographic but hampers representational convergence. In the brain, representations converge most in transmodal, architecturally unconstrained cortex, and topographies are more heritable than representations. They present the ANN results as exemplary and do not extend the principle to artificial systems more broadly.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ResNet-18-derived networks trained with ImageNet contrastive self-supervision, compares different initializations and a spatial wiring-loss condition, and evaluates representational geometry with CKA. It is not presented as a replication of either cited original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Representational similarity differs with the spatial wiring-penalty condition; the text reports a small change across network layers. The paper does not compare alternative representation-similarity metrics as a sensitivity test.

fits_no_version.finding: Across unrelated humans, task-evoked representational geometry (WUC) is more similar in higher-hierarchy cortex despite more divergent topographies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human cortical representational geometry converges across individuals more in transmodal regions, despite idiosyncratic spatial maps.

fits_no_version.finding: Resting-state network geometries are more similar in less myelinated, thicker, later-hierarchy areas.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human representational similarity varies with cortical architectural constraints.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet seed dyads agree on classifications more than TDANN dyads (59.9% vs 54.5%), and agree more with each other than with ground truth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functional (output) agreement across seeds tracks representational rather than topographic similarity.

record.peer_reviewed: bioRxiv preprint; not certified by peer review
record.problems: ANN results use ResNet-18 models and compare a limited set of training conditions; the CKA aggregate is not broken down by network class in the text. The study does not test model-size scaling or alternative similarity metrics. The authors also note that the brain analyses use only 23 task conditions and 25 resting-state networks, and that denser individual sampling is needed to resolve representational geometry more fully.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated ANN class-specific CKA values were available to extract. Functional classification accuracy and agreement results were omitted because they measure output behavior rather than representational similarity. Detailed brain results not directly represented by the listed AI-model claim versions were limited to the illustrative V1 and p9-46v values and aggregate task/rest trends.

untested.parts: No model size or capability sweep; only ResNet-18.
No feature- or subspace-level matching (e.g. unit correlation matching); only global CKA and spatial unit cosine.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations.
No interpretable feature or circuit analysis.
Only one ANN representational metric (unbiased minibatch linear CKA) and in-distribution ImageNet validation inputs.
No plateau test and no test isolating shared data or objectives versus a common model of reality; ANN convergence is high, not far from complete.

missing.what: Unit-level topographic cosine similarity across seeds: 0.36±0.03, decaying strongly with depth (β=-0.260, p=2.0e-10). This bears on V3's 'not the same individual units'.
missing.locator: Results, ANN section; Table 1 topographic similarity; Figure 1C

missing.what: Interaction for geometric similarity, TDANN layer vs ResNet layer (β=-0.137, p=1.7e-4): the layer-wise CKA change differs by wiring condition.
Per-class CKA values for TDANN and ResNet dyads (figure only).

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its ANN component is small (7 dyads per class, ResNet-18 only) and serves mainly as an analogy for the brain analyses. The V7 links in the record were unwarranted and are removed.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size or capability, and no test that alignment between independently trained models rises as models become larger or more capable.
No comparison of vision and language models on paired images and captions.

Tests similarity of representational geometry across random initializations, but not whether the same individual features are shared, nor the specific claim about shared subspaces versus units or bases.
No mapping between models, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Uses different measures for topography and geometry, but does not test whether convergence changes under alternative reasonable representation-similarity measures, their settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.

The ANN results compare representational similarity across wiring-penalty conditions, but do not isolate shared data or objectives as causes against a common model of reality, or establish a plateau. The human results are not tests of AI-model convergence.
